title: Learn JS: Shortest Time
body:
Same network, but now every follow edge u v t takes t units of time to pass an introduction from u to v.

A newbie A wants to be introduced to B as fast as possible. Print the shortest total time from A to B along follow edges, or -1 if B cannot be reached.

Function to complete

Complete shortestTime(members, follower, following, time, a, b). It returns the shortest time from A to B, or -1.

Input reading and printing are handled for you, like on LeetCode. The input format below is what the tests and Custom input use.
inp: Line 1: N. Line 2: the N member IDs. Line 3: E. Next E lines: an edge. Last line: A B. Each edge is follower following time.
out: One integer: the shortest time, or -1.

samples.ex: 7 → 2 → 9 takes 3 + 2 = 5, faster than the direct edge of 7.

py.pre:
from typing import *
import sys, math, collections, heapq, bisect, itertools, functools
from collections import *
py.post:
if __name__ == "__main__":
    _raw = sys.stdin.read(); _t = _raw.split(); _p = 0
    _n = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    members = list(map(int, _t[_p:_p + (_n)])); _p += (_n)
    _e = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    follower = []; following = []; time = []
    for _ in range((_e)):
        follower.append(int(_t[_p + 0]))
        following.append(int(_t[_p + 1]))
        time.append(int(_t[_p + 2]))
        _p += 3
    a = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    b = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    _r = Solution().shortestTime(members, follower, following, time, a, b)
    print(_r)
